newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German third quarter GDP.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German third quarter GDP.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to German third quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data which grew one percent from the quarter before and 2.4 percent year-on-year.

Rob Hayward, Bank of America: "Its a touch stronger than people expected. It is probably within the overall range of exectations. We saw quite a big increase in capital spending. If that is starting to pick up, things look good for 1997. We have to look at industrial production figures and realise they are not very accurate. We have to combine those with the Ifo survey which has shown some rise in business sentiment."

Armin Kayser, SBC Warburg in Frankfurt: "The numbers are a touch higher than expected but I think the government had prepared the markets sufficiently for these results. I don't think that the numbers will affect the markets very much though. The news value of these third quarter numbers is much less than the news value of the October industrial output numbers (down 1.8 percent and released on Tuesday) and so I think the bond market will rather look to the weak industrial output numbers, which helped it on Tuesday, than the stronger GDP numbers, which could pull the market lower." Profit-taking was blamed for a softer bond market opening.

Juergen Pfister, Commerzbank AG: "It is quite clear that the economy is on an upward path but a slow one. We don't see any possibility for a further cut in short-term interest rates as all the Bundesbank's arguments for lower rates -- a weak economy and a strong mark -- are no longer there. We have shifted from a no economic growth scenario to a moderate economic growth scenario so we might see a change in the bond market early next year.
